-119.66100,36.84180.name: Central California IVF Program, Women's Specialty and Fertility Center
-119.66100,36.84180.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Carlos Sueldo, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-71.36200,42.46760.name: Charles River Laboratories
-71.36200,42.46760.desc: Supplies laboratory animals and runs the safety testing that regulators read, which makes it both the largest animal vendor in the world and one of the largest contract testing businesses. The same company breeds the animal and reports the result. Its Safety Assessment division runs the regulated toxicology studies required before anything is given to a person, at sites including Mattawan and Ashland that are among the largest animal facilities in the United States by capacity. Its European breeding network, extended by the Janvier acquisition, supplies the same market on that side of the Atlantic. And it bleeds horseshoe crabs for the lysate used to test injectable drugs for contamination — a business that depends on a wild animal, has no synthetic substitute in widespread use, and is the reason a fifty-million-year-old species now appears in pharmaceutical supply chains.

34.82000,32.01000.name: Volcani Center — Agricultural Research Organization
34.82000,32.01000.desc: Israel's national agricultural research organisation, working on crops for arid and saline conditions and on gene editing in fruit and vegetables. Countries with little water and less arable land have driven a disproportionate share of agricultural biotechnology, because the constraint is severe enough to justify the cost — and the resulting varieties are then useful in places facing the same conditions later.

7.44700,46.94800.name: Pesticide Action Network International
7.44700,46.94800.desc: Tracks pesticide poisoning and campaigns on highly hazardous pesticides worldwide, with the largest published estimates of unintentional poisonings. Herbicide-tolerant crops and herbicide volume are the same subject, and this is the organisation that counts the human cost of the second.

-58.51000,-34.47000.name: Kheiron Biotech
-58.51000,-34.47000.desc: The Argentine laboratory that turned horse cloning into a working industry and then moved past it. It produced eight clones of a single high-value polo mare in 2016, one of the first successful multiple clonings of a performance horse. The animal cost is on the record: of 38 live births from its first clones between 2012 and 2016, made from adult skin cells, almost half had abnormalities of the umbilical cord or placenta, or abnormally bent limbs; results improved when the laboratory switched to bone marrow stem cells. In 2024 it produced five gene-edited foals using CRISPR, based on the genome of a hall-of-fame mare and edited for speed — its scientific director describing the work as designing their genome before they are born. It also states work on pigs for organ transplant compatibility and on cattle for higher protein and shorter coats. Cloning to editing, in one company, in one decade.

80.27070,13.08270.name: LifeCell International
80.27070,13.08270.desc: India's largest cord blood stem cell bank, founded in 2004, and the inventor of a banking model that has since been copied elsewhere in Asia. Ordinary private banking stores a baby's cord blood for that baby, which is of limited use because in the great majority of blood conditions a child's own stored cells cannot be used and a matched donor is needed. Public banking solves the matching problem and is chronically underfunded — India's first public bank stopped accepting donations in 2018 over funding. Community banking sits between them: members pay to join, contribute their child's unit to a shared pool, and may draw from that pool without further payment, with siblings, parents and grandparents covered. The company reported over 75,000 consented units by 2023 and estimates around 60 per cent of the Indian market. Because a match is likeliest within the same ancestry, a national pool of this size is a genuinely different asset from a collection of individual deposits — and it is privately owned.
